newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Road King in 614 mln yuan road projects.
newsitem.headline: Road King in 614 mln yuan road projects.

text.p: Toll road operator Road King Infrastructure Ltd said on Thursday it would invest a total 614.15 million yuan in five highway and bridge projects in the Chinese provinces of Hebei and Shanxi.

Road King said its overall investment in toll road projects would span seven provinces in China, with the total number of projects more than 20, aggregate road mileage reaching 730 kilometers, and total investment amounting to 3.95 billion yuan.
The company said it had signed an agreement with the Shijiazhuang City Communications Department of Hebei province to invest in and operate the National Highway 307 Shijiazhuang to Jinzhou section.
The 40-kilometre highway project, which is already collecting tolls, involves total investment of 330 million yuan. Road King will take a 60 percent stake for 200 million yuan, the statement said.
The company has also signed deals with Shanxi Communications and Construction Development Co in Taiyuan to operates three highways and bridge, which involves an investment of 428.36 million yuan.
Road King will take a 65 percent stake in the project for 278.43 million yuan, it said.
The company said it has also entered into agreement with Shanxi Taiyuan Road and Bridge Co to jointly invest in and operate the provincial highway 104 Taiyuan Ximing to Gujiao Highway section.
The investment for the 41.5-kilometre highway is 226.2 million yuan and Road King will take a 60 percent interest for 135.72 million yuan, it said.
Road King said the company had enough capital to fund all these projects.
"As most of these projects are already open to traffic and collecting tolls, they will provide immediate returns," said the company's finance director Alan Lee in the statement.
The company said it was in a process of arranging a ten-year long term fixed rate note issue, amounting to not less than US$50 million, for further new projects in the future.
Road King shares were unchanged at HK$7.50 in late morning.
